issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task text) refers to a Farm method named printFarmSong()/printFarmSong(), but both the template and the provided solution implement and reference a method named singFarmSong() (and singFarmSongVerse). This name mismatch between the specification and the code can confuse students about which method they are expected to implement and may lead to failing tests or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong()/singFarmSongVerse, or rename the template and solution methods to printFarmSong()/printFarmSongVerse so all materials use the same method name. Ensure the Main example and task descriptions are updated accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to a method named printFarmSong() to play/print the farm song, while both the template and the solution use the method name singFarmSong(). This mismatch between 'printFarmSong' (problem) and 'singFarmSong' (template & solution) can confuse students about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across artifacts. Either change the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong(), or rename the template/solution method to printFarmSong() (and/or add a public printFarmSong() that delegates to the existing singFarmSong()) so students see the same identifier in instructions and code.
